related_questions.question: How long should you stay home once you test positive for COVID?
related_questions.snippet: You should isolate for at least 5 days counting from the day you began feeling sick (Day 0 is the day you began feeling sick; Day 1 is the next day). If you have no symptoms, then isolate for 5 full days after the day you tested positive (Day 0 is the day you took your positive test; Day 1 is the day after).
related_questions.title: What to Do If You Test Positive for COVID-19 - CDPH

related_questions.question: How long are you contagious after you test positive for COVID-19?
related_questions.snippet: While people become less contagious over time, they are still contagious with COVID for an average of eight days. That may vary depending on factors including underlying health conditions and the severity of illness.
related_questions.title: How Long Am I Contagious? - Yale New Haven Hospital

related_questions.question: What to do immediately after testing positive for COVID?
related_questions.snippet: If your COVID-19 test is positive Monitor your symptoms. If you have any emergency warning signs, seek emergency care immediately. Seek health care right away for treatment if you have risk factors for severe illness. Treatment may be an option to make your symptoms less severe and shorten the time you are sick.
related_questions.title: Testing for COVID-19 - CDC

related_questions.question: Can I go to work if I have COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: It's not recommended to go to work if you have COVID-19. Public health organizations advise that you should stay home and away from others to prevent the spread of the virus, especially if you have symptoms.
In California, if you test positive for COVID-19 and have symptoms, you must be excluded from the workplace until:
24 hours have passed with no fever, Symptoms are mild and improving, and No new symptoms develop.
Additionally, your employer is required to:

list.snippet: Investigate and respond to COVID-19 cases or close contacts.
Notify employees and independent contractors about potential exposure.
Offer testing at no cost to employees who had close contact at work.
